headline: DOE Admits Planning Gaps as Visayas Outages May Persist Into 2027
seoTitle: DOE Admits Planning Gaps Behind Visayas Grid Outages
seoDescription: Energy Secretary Sharon Garin acknowledged planning gaps as the Visayas grid faces continued alert risks and long-term fixes may not arrive before 2028.
deck: The Energy Department told lawmakers that near-term measures may reduce but not eliminate grid alerts, while durable capacity additions could take until 2028.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: Energy Secretary Sharon Garin acknowledged planning failures behind recurring Visayas grid shortages during a joint congressional hearing in Bacolod City.

GMA Integrated News reported that even with planned interventions, the Department of Energy's best-case 2027 outlook includes at least one red alert and 19 yellow alerts. These are projections, not a guarantee of specific outages.
The House of Representatives confirmed that the hearing examined recurring red and yellow alerts and their effects on households and businesses.

sections.heading: What the government says it can do
paragraphs: Garin said the department is pursuing battery storage paired with solar capacity and considering power barges as immediate measures. She also said long-term solutions are unlikely before 2028.
The recent alert conditions were linked to forced outages at multiple generating plants. Imports from neighboring grids were not enough to close the shortfall, according to the hearing account.
The hearing does not by itself deliver new capacity. Timelines, procurement, financing and the performance of proposed stopgap measures remain unresolved.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: Unreliable electricity raises costs for households, hospitals, small businesses and manufacturers across the Visayas. It can also disrupt telecommunications, water systems and local government services.

Consumers should continue to monitor National Grid Corporation of the Philippines and local distribution utility advisories. FMB News first reported the current cycle of Visayas grid stress on August 12.
